tenancy.intro: Things the landlord may bring that are not in your files yet. We list them so you are not surprised at the first court meeting. Answer each one.
tenancy.note: The landlord can make a claim back against you, up to 3 days before the first court meeting. Your evidence list is your answer to it.

questions.q: Could the landlord have their own photos of the flat or furniture, taken after you left?
questions.hint: Your own dated move-out photos or video are the answer. Keep them.
questions.they: Photos of the flat or furniture taken after you left
questions.reply: Your own dated move-out photos or video of the same rooms and items.

questions.q: Has the landlord sent, or could they get, a repair or cleaning invoice?
questions.hint: Ask for it in your written request. The court has a form where each fault and its cost is listed.
questions.reply: Your move-in and move-out photos of the same item, and any wear and tear clause in the agreement.

questions.q: Did you sign an inventory or handover form?
questions.hint: Check your agreement for an inventory clause. Get your copy. If it lists the item, it matters either way.
questions.they: The inventory or handover form you signed
questions.reply: Your copy of the form, plus dated photos of the item at move-in and move-out.

questions.q: Were there any other agreed conditions, spoken or in messages on any channel? Cleaning, repainting, bills, keys.
questions.hint: Check SMS, email and other apps you used with them. Anything agreed can change what they can hold back.
questions.they: Messages or words showing other conditions you agreed to
questions.reply: The messages where each condition was set and where you met it, in date order.

questions.q: Did anyone else see the handover? A friend, mover or agent.
questions.hint: Write down their name. You can name them as a witness later.
questions.reply: Your own witness, if anyone was with you. Their name and what they saw.

questions.q: Did you accept any deduction, even in passing?
questions.hint: If yes, say how much and when. It changes the amount you claim.
questions.they: Your own words accepting a deduction
questions.reply: The full message thread around that point, so the words are read in order.

goods.intro: Things the seller may bring that are not in your files yet. We list them so you are not surprised at the first court meeting. Answer each one.
goods.note: The seller can make a claim back against you, up to 3 days before the first court meeting. Your evidence list is your answer to it.

questions.q: Could the seller have a signed delivery note, order form or inspection record?
questions.hint: Check what you signed when you ordered or when goods arrived.
questions.they: A delivery note, order form or inspection record you signed
questions.reply: Your copy of what you signed, and dated photos or messages showing what actually arrived.

questions.q: Did the listing or terms say the goods were sold as seen, used, or without warranty?
questions.hint: Re-read the listing and any terms page.
questions.they: Terms saying sold as seen, used, or no warranty
questions.reply: The listing or messages that describe the goods, and the date you first saw those terms.

questions.q: Did you tell the seller about the problem soon after it showed, in writing?
questions.hint: Find the first message where you raised it and its date.
questions.they: No written complaint from you soon after the problem showed
questions.reply: The first message where you raised the problem, with its date, and any photo sent with it.

questions.q: Did anyone else use, repair or open the goods before you complained?
questions.hint: The seller may say the fault came later.
questions.they: Signs that someone else used, repaired or opened the goods
questions.reply: Dated photos of the fault when it first showed, and any repairer's report saying when it started.

questions.q: Did anyone else see the goods, the fault, or the seller's refusal?
questions.hint: Write down their name. You can name them as a witness later.
questions.they: A witness to the delivery, the fault or the refusal
questions.reply: Your own witness. Their name and what they saw.

questions.q: Did you accept a partial refund, repair, replacement or a changed order, even in passing?
questions.hint: If yes, say what and when. It changes the amount you claim.
questions.they: Your own words accepting a refund, repair, replacement or a changed order
questions.reply: The full message thread around that point, so the words are read in order.

questions.q: Did the seller offer a swap, a smaller delivery or a later date, and you said no?
questions.hint: The seller may say you were the one who cancelled. Keep the messages where you said no and why.
questions.they: Their offer of a swap, a smaller delivery or a later date, and your refusal
questions.reply: The messages where you said no and why, and the original order showing what was agreed.

general.intro: Things the other side may bring that are not in your files yet. We list them so you are not surprised at the first court meeting. Answer each one.
general.note: The other side can make a claim back against you, up to 3 days before the first court meeting. Your evidence list is your answer to it.

questions.q: Could the other side have their own photos, records or receipts about this?
questions.hint: Think about what they would show a judge. Keep anything of yours that answers it.
questions.they: Their own photos, records or receipts
questions.reply: Your own dated photos, records or receipts on the same point.

questions.q: Did anything you signed or agreed to limit what you can claim?
questions.hint: Re-read the contract, quote or terms for words like as is, no refund, or a cap.
questions.they: A signed term that limits what you can claim
questions.reply: The contract or terms, and the messages where the deal was set out.

questions.q: Did you tell the other side about the problem in writing, soon after it happened?
questions.hint: Find the first message where you raised it and its date.
questions.they: No written complaint from you soon after it happened
questions.reply: The first message where you raised the problem, with its date.

questions.q: Were there other agreed conditions, spoken or in messages on any channel?
questions.hint: Check SMS, email and other apps you used with them. Anything agreed can change the claim.
questions.they: Messages or words showing other conditions you agreed to
questions.reply: The messages where each condition was set and where you met it, in date order.

questions.q: Did anyone else see what happened?
questions.hint: Write down their name. You can name them as a witness later.
questions.reply: Your own witness. Their name and what they saw.

questions.q: Did you accept any part payment, repair or discount, even in passing?
questions.hint: If yes, say what and when. It changes the amount you claim.
questions.they: Your own words accepting a part payment, repair or discount
questions.reply: The full message thread around that point, so the words are read in order.
